name: Loperamide
summary: Peripheral mu-opioid agonist that slows gut transit and reduces stool output without meaningful CNS effects at usual doses.
mechanism: Agonist at gut mu-opioid receptors — reduces peristalsis, prolongs transit, and increases anal sphincter tone; P-glycoprotein efflux keeps it out of the CNS at normal doses.

dosing.adult: 4 mg initially, then 2 mg after each loose stool

safety.pregnancy: Limited human data; avoid unless clearly needed
safety.lactation: Excreted in breast milk; generally avoid
warnings: High-dose misuse causes QT prolongation/torsades and CNS opioid effects ('poor man's methadone')
Avoid in bloody diarrhea with fever — masks infection
Stop if constipation, abdominal distension, or ileus develops
Not primary therapy in active IBD flares
monitoring: ECG with high-dose or chronic use
safety.overdose: High doses: QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, CNS depression, respiratory depression — medical emergency; ECG monitoring and supportive care

indications: Chronic diarrhea (IBS-D, short bowel syndrome, post-resection)
clinicalPearls: At high doses it can cross the blood-brain barrier and act like an opioid — the basis of both abuse and cardiotoxicity
Symptomatic only — it does not treat the cause; rehydrate and reconsider in fever or bloody stools
good: Fast, safe symptomatic control of watery non-infectious diarrhea
bad: Bloody diarrhea with fever, C. difficile, children under 2, and high-dose or prolonged use

provenance.notes: Curated from standard pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
